Term1: Infections in bone or joint prostheses
Text:
# INFECTIONS IN BONE OR JOINT PROSTHESES

## Empirical therapy before a pathogen is identified is not recommended unless

## patient is clinically unstable.

Some infections may require one or two stage reimplantation. long-term
suppressive antimicrobial therapy or joint removal without replacement may be
options depending on patient's condition. Consult Infectious Diseases
(inpatient) for more information.

## Infectious Disease and Orthopedics consultations are recommended.

If patient has sepsis or is otherwise unstable, empiric treatment before culture
results are obtained may be justified.


References:
Mandell chapter: Orthopedic Implant-Associated Infections
Up-to-Date Article: Prosthetic Joint Infections: Treatment
Osmon et al, Clinical Infectious Diseases (2013) 56.1, e1-25
Sanford keyword: Prosthetic Joint Infection
Therapy:
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5g IV q6h [R] <OR> cefepime 2g IV q12h

 <AND> 

vancomycin 15 mg/kg q12h [R]

\*in selected cases, oral therapy may be recommended in conjunction with infectious diseases

\*\*Obtain MRSA nares on admission
